Subject: Science
Grade: 10th
Topic: Reproduction in Plants and Animals
Standard: MS-LS1-4 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes
Assessment Title: Survival by Design: Plant and Animal Reproductive Strategies
Overview:
Students will deepen their understanding of reproductive adaptations by designing and presenting a detailed case study on a specific plant or animal, showcasing how its structures and/or behaviors optimize reproductive success.
Assessment Breakdown:
1. Pre-Assessment (Formative)
KWL Chart: Students fill in "Know" and "Want to Know" sections about plant/animal reproduction. This helps gauge understanding and activates inquiry.
Interest Survey: Students express interest in certain types of organisms, influencing project choice.

Notes for Teacher:
Use this survey alongside a brief explanation of the project to build excitement.
While you can't accommodate every choice, the results will help with resource suggestions and potential groupings.
The "extra questions" offer insight into learning profiles for differentiation.


2. Research & Analysis
Focus: Students choose a plant OR animal for the project
Guiding Questions:
What are the key reproductive structures or behaviors of your organism?
How do these adaptations directly contribute to reproductive success (seed dispersal, pollination, survival of offspring, etc.)?
What challenges does your organism face in its environment, and how do the adaptations overcome those?
Differentiated Resources: Provide text sets at varying levels, videos, reputable websites (National Geographic, science museums, etc.)
3. Project Design (Choice & UDL)
Option 1: Visual Model + Explanation
Students create a 3D model (physical or digital) of their organism highlighting key structures.
Accompanying written or oral explanation details how the structures function in reproduction and link to scientific evidence.
Option 2: "Nature Documentary"
Students create a short video showcasing their organism "in the wild," narrating the reproductive behaviors/adaptations
Emphasis on clear explanations, scientific terminology, and visuals from reputable sources.
Option 3: Scientific Poster + Presentation
Students create a detailed infographic-style poster highlighting the organism, its adaptations, and supporting research.
They give a short presentation to the class expanding on their findings.
4. Assessment Rubric (focus on standards, depth of knowledge)
Mastery: Clear explanation of complex adaptations, links to increased reproductive success, strong evidence, effective presentation/model
Proficient: Understanding of basic adaptations, sufficient evidence, organized presentation
Approaching Proficiency: Demonstrates effort in researching adaptations, incomplete explanations, emerging presentation skills.
Types of Knowledge & Processes Assessed:
Factual: Identification of structures/behaviors
Conceptual: Understanding of adaptation purposes, cause-effect relationship to reproduction
Procedural: Research skills, model building, or video/poster creation
Metacognitive: Option for reflection on learning process
Additional Notes:
Peer Feedback: Include a peer feedback phase using the rubric
ELL Support: Sentence starters, translated key terms, option for some use of the home language.
Project Extensions:
Comparison of two contrasting organisms.
Engineering challenge: Design a solution inspired by a reproductive strategy.
